key: in a small town runs a protection racket
name: ch19_dada_pandal_story
alt: A heavyset local strongman stands proudly in front of a festival pandal serving food to the street, while a thought bubble shows how he sees himself: a protector with his arms around his people.
scene: A wide street-level view of a small-town Indian market lane during Ganesh Chaturthi, evening, strings of marigold-coloured bulbs zigzagging overhead. On the LEFT, two modest market stalls, a vegetable cart and a cloth shop, with their owners (a thin older man in a vest and a woman in a green sari) each holding out a small white envelope; a dashed line runs from the envelopes towards the centre, quiet and almost hidden. In the CENTRE, the local strongman, a broad man in his forties with a thick moustache, a white kurta, gold chain and a red tilak, stands chest out in front of a large festival pandal with a scalloped orange canopy, one hand resting on a huge steel pot of food. Beside him a helper ladles food onto leaf plates for a short line of neighbours: a schoolboy, a grandmother and a labourer in a towel turban. Above the strongman floats a large rounded thought bubble showing his inner picture of himself: the same man, smiling warmly, with his arms spread around three small figures as if sheltering them, a little heart above. Inside the bubble a bold label reads "MY PEOPLE". Warm festival light, a gently wry mood: the outside story and the inside story are both visible, and the inside one is the one he believes.

key: Ask a friend in Bengaluru why he bought
name: ch19_suv_two_reasons
alt: A man beside his new large SUV says it is for family safety, while a smaller thought bubble shows the real nudge, a colleague with the same car, and a salesman pitches a warranty with a family-safety shield.
scene: A bright midday scene in a Bengaluru apartment parking lot with a rain tree and a security booth in the background. In the CENTRE, a big boxy SUV in teal, parked and gleaming. Standing in front of it, a man in his mid-thirties (light blue shirt, chinos, car key in hand) gestures warmly. From his mouth rises a large white speech bubble on the LEFT showing his stated reason: a small family of four in the SUV driving along a winding hill road lined with coffee bushes and a little shield icon. Above that speech bubble a bold label reads "SAID". Higher and to the RIGHT, a smaller, fainter dotted thought bubble shows the real nudge: a colleague in an office lanyard standing proudly beside an identical SUV, with a small thumbs-up. Above this bubble a bold label reads "REAL". On the far RIGHT, a young warranty salesman in a neat grey shirt holds up a brochure card showing only a shield with a family inside it, leaning in politely, clearly speaking to the "SAID" reason and not the "REAL" one; the owner is nodding at him. A small green tick near the brochure shows the pitch is landing. Clear daylight, friendly and lightly humorous mood.

key: A flat owner in Pune hears that his tenant
name: ch19_tenant_sweets_visit
alt: A landlord arrives at his tenants' door with a box of sweets and praise instead of waving the lock-in clause, and a small calendar shows the family deciding to stay.
scene: An interior doorway view of a Pune apartment, late afternoon. On the LEFT, the flat owner, a grey-haired man around sixty in a cream kurta and spectacles, stands at the open door holding out a pink-and-gold box of sweets with both hands, a gentle smile on his face. A folded rental agreement sticks out of his kurta pocket, unused, with a small padlock icon on it. In the doorway on the RIGHT side stands the tenant family: a father in his thirties in a checked shirt, a mother in a yellow salwar kameez holding a toddler, and a schoolgirl peeking from behind; they look surprised and touched. Behind them, a few half-packed cardboard boxes sit in the hallway. On the wall beside the door hangs a calendar with the 5th of each month circled with small ticks, showing years of rent paid on time. Above the scene, between the two groups, a bold label reads "BEST TENANTS". In the top RIGHT corner, a small inset bubble shows the same hallway one week later: the cardboard boxes unpacked and flat, a potted plant back on the shelf, and a green tick, with a small label "STAYS". Warm, soft light and a gracious, respectful mood.

key: plays loud music past midnight in your
name: ch19_midnight_music_request
alt: A split picture at midnight: on the left a complaint about irritating music starts a shouting match; on the right a gentle mention of a father's heart check-up gets the volume turned down.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, both halves showing the same Chennai apartment corridor at midnight, with a dark window showing a crescent moon and a wall clock at twelve. A teenage boy in a hoodie and shorts stands in his doorway, a big speaker behind him pumping music notes into the corridor. LEFT panel: the neighbour, a man in his forties in a white vest and veshti, points a finger at the boy with a frown; the boy folds his arms and scowls back, and jagged red lightning lines cross between them; the music notes keep pouring out. Above the left panel a bold label reads "FEUD". RIGHT panel: the same neighbour stands with an open, tired face and his hands gently together; a small inset bubble beside him shows an elderly father lying awake in bed, with a small heart symbol and a calendar page marked for the morning. The boy has turned and is reaching back to the speaker volume knob, the music notes shrinking to almost nothing, his head bowed slightly in apology. Above the right panel a bold label reads "SORRY". Quiet night mood with warm corridor light; the contrast between the two halves is the whole point.

key: A small NGO in Kolkata cannot afford a
name: ch19_ngo_singer_fee
alt: An NGO organiser hands a classical singer a letter offering to send her modest fee to a music school for blind children, and the singer arrives with two students.
scene: A gentle scene in a Kolkata home music room, morning light through tall green-shuttered windows. On the LEFT, the NGO organiser, a young woman in a simple cotton sari with a cloth shoulder bag, holds out an open handwritten letter with both hands, eager and respectful. In the CENTRE, the classical singer, a woman in her fifties in a red-bordered white sari with a large red bindi, sits on a floor cushion beside a tall tanpura, reading the letter with a moved, softening face, one hand on her heart. From a small envelope marked with a rupee symbol near the letter, a dashed amber arrow curves to the RIGHT, where a small building stands: a modest school with a blue door, a little sign showing musical notes, and two children outside, one holding a white cane. Above the arrow a bold label reads "IN YOUR NAME". In the bottom RIGHT, a small inset bubble shows the later fundraiser stage: the singer on a low platform with two young students beside her, one with a harmonium and one with tabla, and a small audience of three heads in the foreground. Warm, quiet, dignified mood; the fee is not haggled, it is turned into something she already cares about.

key: A housing society treasurer in Noida finds
name: ch19_society_penalty_notice
alt: A housing society treasurer sends a stern penalty notice by phone, and six previously reliable flat owners gather together drafting a complaint.
scene: A wide view of a Noida housing society courtyard at dusk, a tall apartment block in the background with six lit windows highlighted in warm amber. On the LEFT, the society treasurer, a balding man in his fifties in a striped shirt and spectacles, sits at a small plastic table under the block's entrance with a thick ledger, typing on his phone with a stern, set jaw. From his phone a large white message bubble flies up and to the right, showing a red stamp-style word and a small lift icon with a rupee sign; inside the bubble a bold label reads "FINAL". Dashed lines shoot from this bubble to each of the six amber windows. On the RIGHT, under a tree, six residents have gathered in a tight huddle around a garden bench: a woman in a sari with a phone, a retired man in a cap, a young couple, a man in office clothes and a woman in a kurta. They lean over a sheet of paper on the bench, one of them writing, others pointing, faces annoyed and determined. On the paper a bold label reads "COMPLAINT". A small calendar beside them shows years of ticks, hinting that these were people who always paid on time. Cool evening light, tense mood: being loudly right has created a faction.

key: A kirana shop owner in Mysuru has a
name: ch19_kirana_credit_book
alt: A kirana shop owner hands the credit book to a disputing customer and lets him decide the amount; the customer remembers his son picking up the rice and pays.
scene: A close, warm view across the wooden counter of a small Mysuru kirana shop, shelves behind stacked with rice sacks, oil tins and glass jars of lentils. On the RIGHT behind the counter stands the shop owner, a man in his sixties in a white shirt and a dhoti, with a calm smile, pushing an open red cloth-bound credit book across the counter towards the customer with one hand, and gesturing with the other palm open, as if to say the choice is yours. Above the shop owner a bold label reads "YOU DECIDE". On the LEFT, the regular customer, a man in his fifties in a mustard shirt and spectacles, holding a cloth bag, stands with one finger on his chin, eyes turned upward in thought. Above his head floats a thought bubble showing a memory: a teenage boy in a school uniform carrying a sack of rice out of this same shop. In the customer's other hand, already half held out, are three folded hundred-rupee notes, with a small quoted tag "Rs 300". A small green tick floats between the notes and the book. A young shop assistant in the background, holding a pencil, looks sheepish. Soft afternoon light, friendly, trusting mood.

key: On a long-distance train, a stranger in
name: ch19_train_bag_trust
alt: On a sleeper train, a stranger walks off to the pantry car after trusting his neighbour with his bag, and the neighbour guards that bag more carefully than his own.
scene: An interior view of an Indian sleeper-class train compartment, side-on, with blue berths, a barred window showing passing green fields and electric poles, and a steel ladder to the upper berth. On the RIGHT, the stranger, a man in his forties in a brown sweater and trousers, walks away down the aisle towards a sign pointing to the pantry car, glancing back over his shoulder with a relaxed, friendly wave; he carries only his wallet. On the berth in the CENTRE sits his big maroon travel bag, unchained, with no lock. Beside it sits the narrator, a young man in a grey T-shirt and track pants, who has turned his whole body towards the stranger's bag, one protective hand resting on it, eyes alert and fixed on the aisle. A large shield-shaped glow outlines the maroon bag, and above it a bold label reads "TRUSTED". On the LEFT, the narrator's own small black backpack lies forgotten under the berth, half open, with a phone charger poking out, and a small question mark beside it to show he is paying it no attention. A tea seller with a kettle passes in the far background. Daylight through the windows, calm, gently comic mood.
